page: Amazon Web Services c7i.metal-24xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by 4th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (model 8488C). The host provides unvirtualized access to 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated execution threads running at a base clock of 3.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 105 MB of shared L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) alongside AVX-512 instruction sets, accelerating dense mathematical operations and specialized deep learning tasks without requiring discrete hardware accelerators.

System memory consists of 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. The configuration includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for non-volatile persistence. Network connectivity is delivered over a 38 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results show top-tier computational capabilities, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,986.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 88,113.34. Extended cryptographic performance is high, with PassMark encryption scoring 90,714.75.

Execution throughput remains robust in parallel workflows such as Clang software compilation (58,663.0) and ray tracing (92,269.0). In-memory caching operations via Redis reach 104.57 million SET operations per second, complemented by static web throughput reaching 77.29 GB/sec. Large model CPU inference displays moderate token generation speeds, such as 35.37 tokens per second on 7B parameter models, though prompt pre-fill rates remain competitive due to vector acceleration.

The c7i.metal-24xl is targeted at high-concurrency enterprise workloads requiring dedicated bare-metal execution, including high-throughput web serving, parallel build farms, batch processing, CPU-based machine learning inference, and low-latency database engines.
